target.title: feat(sessions): create concise titles for saved sessions
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fix classification: Root-cause feature completion for opt-in model-created session titles.
- Root cause: Saved sessions had no durable generated-title source of truth, so session lists fell back to manual names, first user message snippets, or session ids.
- Why this is root-cause fix: `autoTitle` is created once in the reply lifecycle, stored on the session entry, preserved without refreshing session activity, cleared with reset/rollover state, and projected to gateway/Control UI instead of being recomputed by display fallbacks.
- Patch quality notes: The broad catches are intentional isolation for a non-blocking background title task; failures log or no-op instead of interrupting the user reply. The `null`/`false` returns are explicit skip/no-title states for invalid, absent, stale, manually titled, or unreadable sessions.

Why does this matter now?

- Why it matters / User impact: Users with many saved sessions only had manual names, first-message fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, so session history was hard to scan and search. When `sessionTitle.enabled` is true, users can identify conversations by concise stored titles instead of first-message snippets or ids.

What is the intended outcome?

- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the scoped code update after focused validation, local real gateway proof, Control UI visual proof, and passing local ClawSweeper review; maintainer product/privacy/auth acceptance remains maintainer-owned before merge.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- What did NOT change: No unrelated behavior, no default enablement, no migration/backfill, no manual rename UI, no channel/provider/plugin capability change, no agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior change, and no ConfigIO or generic session-store merge policy change.
- Out of scope: Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capability changes, agent-facing `sessions_list` behavior, ConfigIO typing, generic session-store merge policy, and test-project routing.

What does success look like?

Enabled sessions with enough direct user turns get one bounded stored title; manual titles and stale async writes prevent overwrite; reset/new/rollover clears generated titles while preserving manual display names and session activity ordering; gateway and Control UI rows can display and search the generated title.

What should reviewers focus on?

- Architecture / source-of-truth check: `autoTitle` is persisted as session metadata and projected outward; gateway and UI do not maintain a second title source. Runtime auth selection for this path is kept behind internal runtime code so the public runtime-auth helper contract is not expanded.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan: Related context is tracked in #89705. This update is scoped to the existing PR branch for #77165 and does not open a competing new PR or broaden the public provider-auth helper contract.

## Linked context

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: feat(web-search): expose Brave Goggles for custom search filtering and ranking
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Brave Search supports [Goggles](https://search.brave.com/help/goggles), a [query-time DSL](https://brave.com/static-assets/files/goggles.pdf) that redefines how results are ranked at the index level (not client-side post-filtering), but OpenClaw's `web_search` tool has no way to pass them.
- Why it matters: Agents can construct task-specific rules at query time to scope grounding content — e.g. restrict to academic sources, boost official docs over SEO tutorials, suppress low-signal domains — without burning API quota and context window on irrelevant results. The DSL supports site/URL pattern matching (`$site=`, `$inurl=`, wildcards) and ranking actions (`$boost=N`, `$downrank=N`, `$discard`). Rules can be passed inline (newline-separated) or referenced by hosted URL ([quickstart](https://github.com/brave/goggles-quickstart)). Goggles work on both Brave endpoints OpenClaw uses: web search and [llm-context](https://docs.openclaw.ai/brave-search).
- What changed:
  - Added `goggles` string parameter to the Brave tool schema (`src/agents/tools/web-search.ts`) with a self-contained description including DSL syntax and examples so the agent can use it without reading docs
  - Wired `goggles` through to both web and llm-context URL builders
  - Added Brave-only provider validation (`unsupported_goggles` error for non-Brave providers)
  - Included `goggles` in cache keys (different goggles = separate cache entries)
  - Updated `docs/tools/web.md` with paired Goggles + Perplexity examples for domain filtering
  - Updated `docs/brave-search.md` with parameter table entry and usage notes
- What did NOT change (scope boundary):
  - Per-query only — no config schema changes (goggles is not static config)
  - No news search support (OpenClaw doesn't use that endpoint)
  - No changes to other providers
  - No test infrastructure changes

- [x] Feature

- [ ] Chore/infra

- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

None

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `web_search` tool gains an optional `goggles` string parameter (Brave provider only)
- Non-Brave providers return an `unsupported_goggles` error if `goggles` is passed
- Different goggles values produce separate cache entries

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No new endpoints — goggles is appended as a query parameter on existing Brave web search and llm-context API calls.
- Command/tool execution surface changed? Minimal — adds one optional string parameter to an existing tool; no new tool or command.
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any
- Runtime/container: Node 22+
- Model/provider: Brave Search API
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): Brave API key configured

### Steps

1. `pnpm build` — no TS errors
2. `pnpm test -- web-search.test` — all 40 tests pass
3. `pnpm check` — clean
4. Live API: inline goggles (`$discard\n$site=docs.rs\n$site=rust-lang.org`) returned only docs.rs and rust-lang.org results on both web search and llm-context endpoints

### Expected

- Build, tests, and format all pass
- Live queries with goggles return results scoped to the specified rules

### Actual

- All pass as expected

### Examples

```
// Restrict to trusted academic sources
goggles: "$discard\n$site=arxiv.org\n$site=*.edu\n$site=huggingface.co"

// Prioritize docs, suppress blog spam
goggles: "/docs/*$boost=5\n/blog/*$downrank=5"

// Boost actual source code on GitHub
goggles: "$boost=5,site=github.com,inurl=/blob/"
```

## Evidence

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: build pass, all 40 web-search tests pass, format clean, live API calls with inline goggles on both web search and llm-context endpoints
- Edge cases checked: non-Brave provider with goggles (returns `unsupported_goggles` error), cache key differentiation with different goggles values
- What you did **not** verify: hosted goggle URL (only inline rules tested)

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes — new optional parameter, no breaking changes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert the commit; goggles parameter is additive-only
- Files/config to restore: none
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: `unsupported_goggles` errors appearing for Brave provider (would indicate provider detection issue)

## Risks and Mitigations

Low — additive optional parameter on existing Brave API calls; no behavior change when goggles is not supplied.

## Summary

- Problem: Hook completion and error system events were always enqueued to the default agent main session, even when the hook ran against another agent.
- Why it matters: In multi-agent setups this leaked hook summaries, including email-derived content, across agent boundaries.
- What changed: Hook system events now resolve the effective target agent and enqueue to that agent's main session; tests now assert `hooks`-targeted events stay out of the default session.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Hook execution, delivery behavior, and wake-hook routing were not otherwise changed.

target.title: fix(matrix): normalize message fields and deduplicate streaming m.replace events for CLI display
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Matrix `message read` and `message pins` CLI output renders completely empty tables — all four columns (Time, Author, Text, Id) are blank because the formatter doesn't recognize Matrix-native field names. Additionally, Matrix blocked streaming produces one `m.replace` event per edit chunk in the room timeline, so `readMatrixMessages` returns 8+ intermediate edits per message, flooding the table with stale in-progress versions. **Problem 1 — blank table**: Matrix plugin returns messages with fields `eventId` / `sender` / `body` / `timestamp:number`, but the shared CLI formatter `renderMessageList` expects `id` / `authorTag` / `content` / `ts:ISOString`. Zero field overlap → all rows blank. **Problem 2 — streaming noise**: Each `m.replace` edit chunk is a real event in the Matrix timeline. Without dedup, a single blocked-stream response produces 8+ rows of intermediate edits plus the now-stale original. ## Why This Change Was Made 1. **`tool-actions.ts`**: Added `normalizeMatrixMessagesForFormatter()` — maps Matrix-native fields (`eventId` → `id`, `sender` → `authorTag`, `body` → `content`, `timestamp:number` → `ts:ISOString`) additively. Original fields are preserved so `--json` consumers keep the full Matrix payload. `listPins` preserves the raw `events` field alongside the new formatter-friendly `pins` field. 2. **`summary.ts`**: `summarizeMatrixRawEvent` now prefers `m.new_content` over `content.body` for `m.replace` events — the outer `content.body` is a fallback string for clients that don't understand edits, while `m.new_content` carries the authoritative edit body per the Matrix spec. 3. **`messages.ts`**: Added `m.replace` dedup in `readMatrixMessages` — uses timestamp comparison with `event_id` lexicographic tie-break, correct for both backward and forward pagination. Filters out `m.replace` events that lack `m.new_content` (invalid per Matrix spec). Validates that the `m.replace` sender matches the original event sender — cross-sender replacements do not suppress the original message. Both changes are Matrix-plugin-internal. No shared formatter, other channel, or SDK contract changes. **Note on `--json` semantics**: Dedup operates at the payload level in `readMatrixMessages`, so all consumers (CLI text, `--json`, agent tool results) receive the deduped `messages` array. ## What

Adds a bullet to the Timeouts section of `docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` documenting the idle-timeout circuit breaker introduced in #76345.

## Why

The existing Timeouts section explains that individual model requests abort on idle timeout, but says nothing about what happens when idle timeouts repeat. The circuit breaker — which halts further retries after 5 consecutive idle timeouts without completed model progress — is currently undocumented. Users who hit the `[idle-timeout-circuit-breaker-tripped]` error in logs have no docs to explain what they're seeing or why it fired.

## Accuracy

All claims in the added bullet are sourced directly from `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/idle-timeout-breaker.ts` and the CHANGELOG entry for #76345:
- Cap of 5: `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_IDLE_TIMEOUTS_BEFORE_OUTPUT = 5`
- Reset condition: `completedModelProgress` (completed text or tool-call progress), not partial output tokens
- Scope: fires across auth-profile retries inside the same embedded run
- Incident numbers: from the original issue #76293 report

target.title: fix(voice-call): fix telnyx streaming transcription stt in conversation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbound Telnyx PSTN calls went silent because Telnyx requires an explicit `POST /v2/calls/{call_control_id}/actions/streaming_start` command to start WebSocket media streaming. Additionally, Telnyx WebSocket frames are structured differently than Twilio frames and were not being parsed.

Two additional issues were addressed after initial review:

1. **Security (ClawSweeper P1):** The original implementation sent a static, reusable stream URL with no per-call credential. A rogue client that knew an active `call_control_id` could inject fake audio. Fixed in commit 2 by embedding a per-call cryptographic token.

2. **Availability (ClawSweeper P1):** `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` returned `true` based on URL+path alone, not on whether the `MediaStreamHandler` was actually initialized. Fixed in commit 2 to match Twilio's readiness contract.

---

## Technical Changes

### Commit 1 — Core streaming path
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: Supported classic `streamPath` configurations, public URL storage, and stream URL resolution.
- `manager/events.ts`: Injected the classic `streamUrl` into `answerCall` parameters for Telnyx inbound calls (bypassed if `realtime` is enabled).
- `media-stream.ts`: Added support for pluggable WS message parsers and implemented `parseTelnyxMediaMessage()` to decode Telnyx inbound WebSocket frames.
- `runtime.ts`: Registered `parseTelnyxMediaMessage` and configured streaming options when initializing Telnyx.
- `cli.ts`: Updated self-check CLI output logic.

### Commit 2 — Security + availability hardening (addresses ClawSweeper P1 findings)
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: `getClassicStreamUrl(callControlId)` now appends a per-call `?token=<crypto.randomBytes(16).base64url>`. `isValidStreamToken(callId, token)` performs constant-time comparison via `safeEqualSecret` (same utility as Twilio). `isConversationStreamConnectEnabled()` now gates on `this.mediaStreamHandler !== null`, matching Twilio's readiness contract exactly.
- `webhook.ts`: `shouldAcceptStream` callback now validates Telnyx stream tokens the same way Twilio tokens are already validated — unauthenticated WebSocket upgrades are rejected with `1008 Unauthorized stream`.
- `runtime.ts`: Wires `mediaStreamHandler` into `TelnyxProvider` after initialization so the readiness gate is populated.
- `events.ts`: Fixed `TS2352` type assertion (cast through `unknown` as required by TypeScript for non-overlapping interface casts).

---

## Security Fix — How Token Auth Works

```
answerCall()
  └─ getClassicStreamUrl("CA-xyz")
       └─ generates token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("base64url")
       └─ stores token in Map<callControlId, token>
       └─ returns "wss://example.com/voice/stream?token=<token>"

WebSocket upgrade arrives at /voice/stream?token=<t>
  └─ shouldAcceptStream({ callId: "CA-xyz", token: "<t>" })
       └─ telnyx.isValidStreamToken("CA-xyz", "<t>")
            └─ safeEqualSecret(storedToken, providedToken)  ← constant-time
            └─ true → stream accepted
            └─ false → ws.close(1008, "Unauthorized stream")
```

---


target.title: fix(slack): bridge presentation capabilities and renderPresentation through channel outbound facade
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack users sending portable presentations would receive only plain-text fallback content because the Slack channel facade did not expose its native presentation renderer. This affected Block Kit text, dividers, buttons, selects, card receipts, and callback delivery.

Closes #95440

## Why This Change Was Made

The Slack facade now advertises one shared capability contract and lazily delegates native rendering to the Slack outbound adapter. The adapter preserves authored block order and visible payload text, enforces Slack's text/action/option/message limits, falls back without dropping content, and ignores callbacks generated by URL-only buttons (including already-posted legacy buttons). Core receipt classification now recognizes semantic presentations and non-empty rendered presentation blocks before plain text.

## User Impact

Slack presentation payloads now render as native Block Kit cards with working controls and `card` receipts. Unsupported or oversized content remains visible as a complete fallback; ordinary non-presentation media and interactive sends retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Existing live Slack proof in this PR and #95440: native Block Kit screenshots, a `receipt.parts[0].kind = "card"` CLI result, and independent production confirmation that bridging this facade path restores buttons and callbacks.
- Focused rebased proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...` across nine core/Slack files — 176 tests passed.
- Fresh autoreview after all fixes: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Full changed gate: Testbox `tbx_01kwpqw5dfdsykccvz0923dy0d`, [Actions run 28708979405](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28708979405), exit 0.

target.title: fix(copilot): bound BYOK proxy request bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Copilot BYOK users could have the local provider proxy buffer an unbounded request body before forwarding when the SDK sent an unexpectedly large POST.

## Why This Change Was Made

The BYOK proxy now applies the same bounded request-body guard pattern used by other plugin HTTP ingress paths. The intended BYOK proxy request-body cap is 16 MiB with a 30s read timeout; oversized requests are rejected locally with 413 before reaching the guarded upstream fetch.

## User Impact

Users keep the same BYOK provider behavior for normal SDK requests, while malformed or runaway local requests can no longer grow proxy memory without a cap.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): harden bridge imports under concurrent syncs
target.body:
## Summary

- Add bounded retry handling for transient `FsSafeError: path-mismatch` while writing imported memory-wiki source pages.
- Coalesce concurrent bridge imported-source syncs for the same resolved vault/config so `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace` share the same in-flight bridge sync instead of launching duplicate import/index-refresh passes.
- Preserve existing vault safety boundaries for symlink/path-alias and directory-collision cases.
- Rebase the existing PR onto current `origin/main` and keep main's shared guarded page-write path while retaining this PR's imported-source retry and bridge sync coalescing.
- **What did NOT change:** Out of scope and unchanged: no channel delivery, provider routing, plugin-hook contract, gateway method signature, config schema/default, or broad session model change; the behavior change is only the `extensions/memory-wiki` imported-source retry/coalescing path.
- Why it matters / User impact: concurrent memory-wiki bridge imports no longer duplicate expensive import passes or fail the bridge surface on transient filesystem `path-mismatch` races, without weakening path safety.

Related to #91154.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bridge-mode memory-wiki imported-source sync runs through the real OpenClaw gateway surface for `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, `wiki.palace`, and `wiki.bridge.import`; concurrent bridge calls for the same vault/config coalesce to one underlying bridge ingest/index-refresh pass; transient source-page rewrite pressure does not break the gateway or leave the bridge vault inconsistent.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux worktree `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-91828`, exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422`, local `origin/main` ref `6638a575d39dee5e64ecb562695b70affca8f4b4` during the gateway proof. A post-proof daily-fix drift check against `origin/main` `48e8965b1060d61beda1a52d572373a409317498` found no overlapping changed files and `sync_main_required=false`. Runtime used an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway at `/tmp/openclaw-pr91828-runtime-20260703-proof` with `vaultMode=bridge`, `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts=true`, and a public `MEMORY.md` artifact in the isolated workspace. Secrets and gateway tokens are not included in the evidence or this PR body.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-91828-evidence/run-gateway-proof-20260703.mjs"
```

The runner starts an exact-head loopback gateway, calls `wiki.status`, `health`, `wiki.importInsights`, and `wiki.palace`, then launches six concurrent gateway calls (`2 x wiki.status`, `2 x wiki.importInsights`, `2 x wiki.palace`), runs eight `wiki.bridge.import` calls while an external writer repeatedly replaces the generated bridge source page, searches the isolated runtime logs for `path-mismatch`/`FsSafeError`/refusal signals, and finally checks that an unknown-method request fails without destabilizing a follow-up `wiki.status`.

- **Evidence after fix:**


- **Observed result after fix:** `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, `wiki.palace`, and `wiki.bridge.import` all succeed through the real `openclaw gateway call` surface against bridge-mode memory-wiki with one discovered public memory artifact and one generated bridge source page. After a live workspace artifact update, six concurrent gateway calls produced exactly one new bridge ingest log entry, showing that concurrent callers shared one bridge import/index-refresh pass for the same resolved config identity. The atomic source-page rewrite pressure probe did not break imports or final status, and the adjacent unknown-method probe returned a structured gateway error without destabilizing the gateway.
- **What was not tested:** The live race probe did not emit a directly observable `path-mismatch`/`FsSafeError` log signal, so this update does not claim a naturally observed path-mismatch recovery event; it proves the gateway stayed healthy under source-page atomic rewrite pressure and the code-level retry remains bounded to that transient error. I did not rerun the reporter-scale ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload, external channel delivery, or third-party provider/API proof on this head.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 [P1] exact-head real behavior proof for bridge gateway methods and retry/coalescing behavior:** Addressed for the real gateway surface on exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422`. `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, `wiki.palace`, and `wiki.bridge.import` all succeeded against bridge mode with a real public memory artifact; the concurrent six-call probe produced exactly one new ingest entry. Remaining gap: the live rewrite-pressure probe did not naturally surface a `path-mismatch` log/error signal, so that part is disclosed instead of overstated.
- **RF-002 [P1] live/local bridge proof gap:** Addressed with an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway, memory-core + memory-wiki loaded, `vaultMode=bridge`, `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts=true`, and `bridgePublicArtifactCount=1` from an actual workspace `MEMORY.md` artifact.
- **RF-003 [P1] session-state / coalescing identity risk:** Addressed by the implementation and runtime probe. The coalescing key includes vault path/mode, bridge/ingest/render/search/context/obsidian config, and agent default/list workspace identity; the runtime concurrent batch updated the live artifact once and produced a single ingest delta across six gateway calls.
- **RF-004 [P1] stale gateway-load / reporter-scale proof:** Partially addressed and partially disclosed. This update supplies exact-head local gateway proof and fresh focused Vitest results after the rebase/conflict resolution; it does not claim the reporter's ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload was rerun.
- **RF-005 [maintainer decision] merge-risk / canonical retry acceptance:** Still requires maintainer judgment. This rebase keeps current main's shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing; maintainers should make the final broad-vs-narrow canonical merge decision.
- **RF-006 [signal] fresh proof / re-review:** This update replaces stale pre-rebase proof with current-head runtime gateway evidence and records it through the daily-fix verification marker. Remaining proof gaps are explicitly listed in `What was not tested` rather than hidden behind local tests.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- ClawSweeper previously flagged overlap with #94443 on transient `path-mismatch` retry behavior.
- This conflict resolution uses the current main shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` retry behavior for the guarded write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing.
- This avoids restoring a divergent direct write retry path, but it does not override the remaining maintainer choice about broad-vs-narrow canonical merge direction.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** coalesced concurrent imported-source sync for identical bridge config, separate coalescing identity when workspace inputs differ, transient imported-source `path-mismatch` retry, preserved human Notes, and preserved symlink/path-alias + directory-collision refusal.
- **Command:**

```bash
cd "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-91828"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.test.ts \
```

target.title: fix(sessions): exclude done sessions from transcript freshness rollover guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful main sessions (`status: "done"`) can roll over to new session IDs and archive transcript as `.jsonl.reset.*` when the transcript file mtime is slightly newer than the registry `updatedAt`, even though the session completed successfully.
- Problem: `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck` applies the transcript freshness guard to `status: "done"` rows, forcing unnecessary session rotation on the next inbound message.
- Solution: Exclude `status: "done"` from the guard alongside the already-excluded `status: "failed"`, so successful sessions stay reusable.
- What changed: One condition in `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` (core fix), test expectations in 3 test files.
- What did NOT change: `killed`/`timeout` still guarded; `endedAt-only` terminal rows still guarded; no config/API/docs changes.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #99964
- Related #99971 (alternative PR)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

After a main session completes successfully (`status: "done"`), the next user message should reuse the same session. However, when the transcript file's mtime is slightly newer than the session registry's `updatedAt` (which can happen due to filesystem I/O timing — the transcript write may land after the registry update), `hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistry` returns `true`, causing `canReuseSession` to be `false`. This forces a new UUID session and archives the old transcript as `.jsonl.reset.*`.

Three call paths are affected:
1. Gateway agent session admission (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts:1956-1970`)
2. CLI command session resolver (`src/agents/command/session.ts:379-389`)
3. Auto-reply session (`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:548`)

All three use the same shared guard function, so fixing it in one place covers all paths.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck()` now returns `undefined` for `status: "done"` rows, preventing transcript-mtime-based rollover for successful completions.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, branch `fix/done-session-transcript-guard-99964`

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-99964-evidence/full-chain-proof.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.session.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run -t "terminal"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts --run -t "terminal"
```

- Evidence after fix:

```
============================================================
  PR #99964 Full-Chain Live Proof
============================================================

  Session status: done | transcript mtime > registry: YES

  [Layer 1] Guard function (shared by Gateway + CLI + Auto-reply)
    hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistrySync() = false
    => PASS: Guard skipped for done sessions (enables reuse)

  [Layer 2] CLI resolveSession() - proven by passing test
    Test: 'reuses status-done terminal main sessions'
    File: src/commands/agent.session.test.ts
    Assertions: isNewSession=false, sessionId matches original
    => PASS (test suite: 8/8 passed)

  [Layer 3] Gateway handler - proven by passing test
    Test: 'reuses a status-done terminal main session when its transcript is newer'
    File: src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
    => PASS (test suite: 20/20 terminal tests passed)

  [Layer 4] Auto-reply session - proven by passing test
    Test: 'main status-done terminal rows reuse when transcript is newer'
    File: src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts
    => PASS (6/6 terminal tests passed)

  [Behavior Matrix] All 3 call paths, all session states
  +----------------+--------+-------------+----------+-----------+
  | Status         | mtime  | Before fix  | After fix | Guard    |
  +----------------+--------+-------------+----------+---------+
  | done           | > reg  | Rotation    | Reuses   | false    |
  | failed         | > reg  | Reuses      | Reuses   | false    |
  | killed         | > reg  | Rotation    | Rotation | true     |
  | timeout        | > reg  | Rotation    | Rotation | true     |
  | endedAt-only   | > reg  | Rotation    | Rotation | true     |
  +----------------+--------+-------------+----------+---------+

  ALL LAYERS PASSED
```

| Test file | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| `src/commands/agent.session.test.ts` | 8 passed |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (terminal) | 6 passed, 108 skipped |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` (terminal) | 20 passed, 308 skipped |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `status: "done"` sessions with newer transcript mtime no longer trigger session rollover
  2. `failed` sessions remain reusable (existing behavior preserved)
  3. `killed`/`timeout`/`endedAt-only` sessions remain guarded (existing behavior preserved)
  4. All existing tests updated and pass

- What was not tested: Full Gateway with a real remote model provider — the session reuse decision happens before any model call, so mocked model responses in the Gateway tests prove the same code path. All 4 layers (guard function, CLI resolveSession, Gateway handler, auto-reply) are covered.


## Root Cause

In `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck()` (`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts:162-184`):

```
const hasTerminalLifecycle =
    isTerminalSessionStatus(params.entry.status) ||  // "done" is terminal
    resolvePositiveTimestamp(params.entry.endedAt) !== undefined;
if (!hasTerminalLifecycle) { return undefined; }
if (params.entry.status === "failed") {
    // Only "failed" was excluded — "done" fell through to the guard
    return undefined;
}
```

`isTerminalSessionStatus()` includes `"done"`, `"failed"`, `"killed"`, `"timeout"` — but only `"failed"` was excluded from the mtime check, leaving `"done"` (successful completion) unprotected.

**Provenance**: Introduced in `af906225fa` (Fermin Quant, 2026-06-25) as part of PRs #0c9ac48d and #57bed6ae which added the terminal-main transcript freshness guard.

## Alternative Approach Considered

Two approaches were considered:

**Option A (chosen)**: Exclude `status: "done"` from the transcript freshness guard. Minimal change, low risk.

**Option B (not chosen)**: Fix the persistence ordering so transcript mtime never exceeds registry `updatedAt`. This addresses the root cause (filesystem I/O timing), but involves more code paths and complexity. The persistence ordering issue is a known technical debt that could be addressed as a follow-up for other terminal states.

Option A was chosen because:
- It directly fixes the user-facing bug with minimal risk
- It follows the established pattern of excluding `failure` (same exclusion approach)
- The guard remains active for abnormal terminal states (`killed`, `timeout`, `endedAt-only`) where transcript-continuity recovery logic is still important
- A follow-up fix for persistence ordering would benefit all terminal states uniformly

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Successful main-agent sessions will no longer unexpectedly roll over to a new session ID when the transcript mtime is slightly newer than the registry `updatedAt`. The `.jsonl.reset.*` archive pattern will no longer appear for normal successful runs.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Regression Test Plan

- Updated existing test expectation in `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` for `status: "done"` case (now expects reuse instead of rotation)
- Updated existing test expectation in `src/commands/agent.session.test.ts` for `status: "done"` cases (now expects reuse)
- Updated existing test expectation in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` for the default-done case
- `endedAt-only` test cases unchanged (still assert rotation — guard remains active)
- All 3 affected test suites pass

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: status-done with newer transcript (reuse), endedAt-only with newer transcript (rotation), failed with newer transcript (reuse, unchanged), killed/timeout with newer transcript (rotation, unchanged)
- Edge cases checked: main session aliases (canonical, raw, custom) with done status; explicit session-id resume still works
- What you did NOT verify: Full Gateway E2E; real agent run producing the mtime ordering race

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only relaxes session reuse, never tightens
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The shared guard function is the right boundary because all three affected call paths (gateway, CLI, auto-reply) already depend on it. Adding the condition inline is minimal and follows the existing `failed` exclusion pattern.
- **Refactor needed**: No. A follow-up to fix persistence ordering (Option B) could be filed separately.
- **Alternative considered**: Fix persistence ordering so `updatedAt >= transcript mtime`. This is a deeper fix but involves more risk and wasn't necessary for this bug.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Lowest risk**: Only relaxes the guard for successful completions (`status: "done"`). Abnormal terminal states (`killed`, `timeout`, `endedAt-only`) remain fully guarded.
- **Familiar pattern**: Follows the exact same approach as the existing `failed` exclusion.
- **Test coverage**: All 3 call paths covered by existing tests, with updated expectations for the new behavior.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

Fixes #99964

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could see the main agent unexpectedly roll into a new session after a successful completed run when the transcript file mtime was newer than `sessions.json.updatedAt`.

Successful `status: "done"` main sessions now stay reusable when the transcript freshness guard sees a newer transcript mtime. The terminal-main transcript guard still applies to unsafe recovery shapes such as endedAt-only rows and interrupted terminal statuses, so interrupted or ambiguous terminal state can still force rollover.

The fix lives at the session lifecycle guard owner so gateway, CLI command session resolution, and auto-reply admission all share the same decision instead of each caller special-casing successful runs.

Main-agent conversations keep their session id and transcript continuity after successful runs. Users should no longer get surprise reset archives solely because transcript persistence landed after the registry bookkeeping timestamp.

target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? target.title: feat(openshell): add non-secret env config for sandbox creation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenShell sandboxes often need non-sensitive environment variables (API base URLs, model names, regions) at creation time. The OpenShell CLI supports `--env KEY=VALUE` since v0.0.59, but the OpenClaw plugin config had no way to pass these through, forcing users to manually configure env vars after each sandbox recreation.

close #96056

## Why This Change Was Made

Added an optional `env` map to the OpenShell plugin config. When a sandbox is created, each entry is translated to `--env KEY=VALUE` in the `openshell sandbox create` invocation. Empty by default (`{}`), so existing configs are unaffected.

Env key validation is split across two layers:

- **Runtime** (`config.ts` Zod `.superRefine`): rejects empty keys, surrounding whitespace, keys with `OPENSHELL_` prefix, and keys that aren't valid shell identifiers (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`)
- **Manifest** (`openclaw.plugin.json` `propertyNames`): mirrors the same pattern so the Control UI config form rejects invalid keys before save. `normalizeJsonSchema` intentionally strips `propertyNames` during export, so the manifest → runtime schema comparison accounts for this known gap.

## User Impact

Users can configure non-secret env vars in `openclaw.json`:

```json5
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      openshell: {
        enabled: true,
        config: {
          env: {
            MODEL_BASE_URL: "https://api.example.com/v1",
            MODEL_NAME: "gpt-oss-20b",
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Changing env requires sandbox recreation (`openclaw sandbox recreate --all`).

## Evidence

- Tests: 70 tests passing (config + mirror + CLI + backend)
- oxlint: clean
- oxfmt: clean

### Code path — env passed as `--env KEY=VALUE` flags

[`extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts):
```typescript
...Object.entries(this.params.execContext.config.env).flatMap(([key, value]) => [
  "--env",
  `${key}=${value}`,
]),
```

### Config validation — runtime + manifest

Runtime rejects invalid keys (`extensions/openshell/src/config.ts` `superRefine`):

```
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key " FOO" has surrounding whitespace
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key "OPENSHELL_KEY" uses reserved OPENSHELL_ prefix
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key "123invalid" is not a valid environment variable name
```

Manifest schema (`extensions/openshell/openclaw.plugin.json`) validates key patterns:

```
propertyNames: {
  pattern: "^(?!OPENSHELL_)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$",
  minLength: 1
}
```

### Live verification — sandbox printenv

After configuring `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env` and running `openclaw sandbox recreate --all`:

```
$ openclaw sandbox exec -- printenv | grep -E "MODEL_BASE_URL|MODEL_NAME|HOME|PATH"
HOME=/root
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1
MODEL_NAME=gpt-oss-20b
```

The configured env vars are present in the sandbox alongside system defaults.

### When to recreate — docs updated

[`docs/gateway/openshell.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/openshell.md) "When to recreate" section lists `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env`.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openshell/src/config.ts` | Type + Zod schema with key validation + resolver |
| `extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts` | `--env` args in sandbox create |
| `extensions/openshell/openclaw.plugin.json` | Manifest schema with `propertyNames` pattern + uiHints |
| `extensions/openshell/src/config.test.ts` | 70 tests: runtime key validation + manifest `propertyNames` pattern + schema sync (gap-aware) |
| `docs/gateway/openshell.md` | Config table, example, recreate guidance |

## Merge Risk

- **New config surface**: `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env` adds a new openclaw.json option. Follows existing pattern; defaults to `{}` so existing configs unaffected.
- **Env key validation**: Invalid keys rejected at schema parse time, not at sandbox create. Prevents silent failures.
- **Sandbox recreation required**: Env only applied at create time. Documented.
- **No security regression**: Env values passed as `--env KEY=VALUE` argv. Non-secret only, as documented.
- **Backward compatible**: Config is optional. Omitted → same behavior as before.

target.title: fix: exclude done sessions from transcript freshness rollover guard
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Successful main sessions (`status: "done"`) can unnecessarily roll over to new session IDs when the transcript file mtime is slightly newer than the registry `updatedAt`, archiving the old transcript as `.jsonl.reset.*`.

**Solution**: Exclude `status: "done"` from the transcript-newer-than-registry freshness guard in `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck`, matching the existing exclusion for `status: "failed"`.

**What changed**: One condition in `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` — added `|| params.entry.status === "done"` to the existing `failed` exclusion check.

**What did NOT change**: 
- `killed` and `timeout` states still have the freshness guard (correct for interrupted/error sessions)
- No caller code changes needed
- No config, API, or docs changes

Fixes #99964

## What Problem This Solves

After a main session completes successfully (status: "done"), if the transcript file's mtime happens to be newer than the `sessions.json` entry's `updatedAt` timestamp, the next inbound message triggers `hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistry`, which returns `true`. This causes `freshEntry` to become `false` in both the auto-reply and Gateway session resolution paths, forcing a new UUID session and archiving the previous session's transcript.

The mtime/updatedAt ordering can differ due to filesystem I/O timing — the transcript file gets written last by the agent run, and the session registry update may complete slightly before the file write is fully flushed to disk.

## Root Cause

In `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck` (lifecycle.ts:168–172), only `status: "failed"` was excluded from the freshness guard:
- `"failed"` → return undefined (no guard) — correct, retry/recovery
- `"done"` → **fell through** to the mtime check — **bug**
- `"killed"/"timeout"` → have the guard — correct, interrupted states

`isTerminalSessionStatus()` (types.ts:440–444) returns true for all four terminal states (`done`, `failed`, `killed`, `timeout`), but `done` (successful completion) was not handled the same as `failed`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck` now returns `undefined` for `status: "done"` sessions, preventing transcript-mtime-based rollover.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22, OpenClaw 2026.7 development branch (fix/worktree)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/config/sessions/
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal
 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668001277/Projects/github/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-99964

 Test Files  30 passed (30)
      Tests  443 passed (443)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 443 session lifecycle tests pass. The `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck` function now correctly returns `undefined` for `status: "done"` sessions, matching the existing `failed` exclusion.

| Status | Before | After | Expected |
|--------|--------|-------|----------|
| `done` | Freshness guard active → rollover possible | No guard → session reusable | ✅ Fixed |
| `failed` | No guard (excluded) | No guard (unchanged) | ✅ No change |
| `killed` | Guard active | Guard active | ✅ No change |
| `timeout` | Guard active | Guard active | ✅ No change |

**What was not tested**: Full Gateway integration (the fix is a narrow pure logic change with no I/O side effects, well-covered by unit tests).

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk declaration — one-line condition addition, no behavioral change for other terminal states
- [x] Existing test suite passes (443/443 session tests)
- [x] `killed`/`timeout` guards remain active (no behavioral change for interrupted sessions)

## Summary - add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries - add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation - report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config - document the new policy rule in the Policy CLI and plugin reference docs - classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage  ## Policy syntax / evidence / finding contract  Policy syntax added by this PR:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` is an exact, case-sensitive deny-superset rule. An equal-or-stricter policy must include every command required by the baseline deny list. Empty or missing `denyCommands` means this rule is not active.  OpenClaw config evidence collected by policy doctor:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "allowCommands": ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"],       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  The evidence scanner records concrete config entries as:  ```text kind=nodeAllowCommand command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/allowCommands/#2 kind=nodeDenyCommand  command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands/#0 ```  Finding emitted when policy requires a deny but config does not provide it:  ```json {   "checkId": "policy/gateway-node-command-denied",   "severity": "error",   "message": "Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config.",   "path": "openclaw config",   "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "target": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "fixHint": "Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review." } ```  The finding clears when the config deny list contains the required exact command id. `allowCommands` evidence is collected for coverage and context; this PR only enforces the policy deny-superset contract.  ## Real behavior proof  Behavior or issue addressed: Managed policy can now require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be denied in OpenClaw config via `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`. The policy doctor reports the missing config deny and clears once the config denylist covers the policy denylist.  Real environment tested: Windows 11 PowerShell, `C:\src\openclaw-fork` checkout at PR head `cfe901e17963d9fe1833266a2758f125d7a51762`, source-harness invocation of the real policy doctor health checks through `runDoctorLintChecks`. The harness wrote real temporary `openclaw.jsonc` and `policy.jsonc` files under `%TEMP%`; no cloud gateway or Lobster deployment was involved.  Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Ran a Node/tsx source harness from the repo root that imported `registerPolicyDoctorChecks` and `runDoctorLintChecks`. 2. Case `missing-config-deny`: wrote `policy.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]` and `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.allowCommands: ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"]` and no config `denyCommands`. 3. Case `satisfied-config-deny`: wrote the same policy plus `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]`.  Evidence after fix: ```text CASE missing-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-missing-config-deny-Xk9xXX openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] finding.checkId: policy/gateway-node-command-denied finding.severity: error finding.message: Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config. finding.ocPath: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.target: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.requirement: oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.fixHint: Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review. target.title: fix(sessions): exclude done sessions from transcript freshness rollover guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful main sessions (`status: "done"`) can roll over to new session IDs and archive transcript as `.jsonl.reset.*` when the transcript file mtime is slightly newer than the registry `updatedAt`, even though the session completed successfully.
- Problem: `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck` applies the transcript freshness guard to `status: "done"` rows, forcing unnecessary session rotation on the next inbound message.
- Solution: Exclude `status: "done"` from the guard alongside the already-excluded `status: "failed"`, so successful sessions stay reusable.
- What changed: One condition in `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` (core fix), test expectations in 3 test files.
- What did NOT change: `killed`/`timeout` still guarded; `endedAt-only` terminal rows still guarded; no config/API/docs changes.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #99964
- Related #99971 (alternative PR)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

After a main session completes successfully (`status: "done"`), the next user message should reuse the same session. However, when the transcript file's mtime is slightly newer than the session registry's `updatedAt` (which can happen due to filesystem I/O timing — the transcript write may land after the registry update), `hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistry` returns `true`, causing `canReuseSession` to be `false`. This forces a new UUID session and archives the old transcript as `.jsonl.reset.*`.

Three call paths are affected:
1. Gateway agent session admission (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts:1956-1970`)
2. CLI command session resolver (`src/agents/command/session.ts:379-389`)
3. Auto-reply session (`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:548`)

All three use the same shared guard function, so fixing it in one place covers all paths.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck()` now returns `undefined` for `status: "done"` rows, preventing transcript-mtime-based rollover for successful completions.
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, branch `fix/done-session-transcript-guard-99964`

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-99964-evidence/full-chain-proof.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.session.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run -t "terminal"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts --run -t "terminal"
```

- Evidence after fix:

```
============================================================
  PR #99964 Full-Chain Live Proof
============================================================

  Session status: done | transcript mtime > registry: YES

  [Layer 1] Guard function (shared by Gateway + CLI + Auto-reply)
    hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistrySync() = false
    => PASS: Guard skipped for done sessions (enables reuse)

  [Layer 2] CLI resolveSession() - proven by passing test
    Test: 'reuses status-done terminal main sessions'
    File: src/commands/agent.session.test.ts
    Assertions: isNewSession=false, sessionId matches original
    => PASS (test suite: 8/8 passed)

  [Layer 3] Gateway handler - proven by passing test
    Test: 'reuses a status-done terminal main session when its transcript is newer'
    File: src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
    => PASS (test suite: 20/20 terminal tests passed)

  [Layer 4] Auto-reply session - proven by passing test
    Test: 'main status-done terminal rows reuse when transcript is newer'
    File: src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts
    => PASS (6/6 terminal tests passed)

  [Behavior Matrix] All 3 call paths, all session states
  +----------------+--------+-------------+----------+-----------+
  | Status         | mtime  | Before fix  | After fix | Guard    |
  +----------------+--------+-------------+----------+---------+
  | done           | > reg  | Rotation    | Reuses   | false    |
  | failed         | > reg  | Reuses      | Reuses   | false    |
  | killed         | > reg  | Rotation    | Rotation | true     |
  | timeout        | > reg  | Rotation    | Rotation | true     |
  | endedAt-only   | > reg  | Rotation    | Rotation | true     |
  +----------------+--------+-------------+----------+---------+

  ALL LAYERS PASSED
```

| Test file | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| `src/commands/agent.session.test.ts` | 8 passed |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (terminal) | 6 passed, 108 skipped |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` (terminal) | 20 passed, 308 skipped |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `status: "done"` sessions with newer transcript mtime no longer trigger session rollover
  2. `failed` sessions remain reusable (existing behavior preserved)
  3. `killed`/`timeout`/`endedAt-only` sessions remain guarded (existing behavior preserved)
  4. All existing tests updated and pass

- What was not tested: Full Gateway with a real remote model provider — the session reuse decision happens before any model call, so mocked model responses in the Gateway tests prove the same code path. All 4 layers (guard function, CLI resolveSession, Gateway handler, auto-reply) are covered.


## Root Cause

In `resolveTerminalMainSessionTranscriptRegistryCheck()` (`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts:162-184`):

```
const hasTerminalLifecycle =
    isTerminalSessionStatus(params.entry.status) ||  // "done" is terminal
    resolvePositiveTimestamp(params.entry.endedAt) !== undefined;
if (!hasTerminalLifecycle) { return undefined; }
if (params.entry.status === "failed") {
    // Only "failed" was excluded — "done" fell through to the guard
    return undefined;
}
```

`isTerminalSessionStatus()` includes `"done"`, `"failed"`, `"killed"`, `"timeout"` — but only `"failed"` was excluded from the mtime check, leaving `"done"` (successful completion) unprotected.

**Provenance**: Introduced in `af906225fa` (Fermin Quant, 2026-06-25) as part of PRs #0c9ac48d and #57bed6ae which added the terminal-main transcript freshness guard.

## Alternative Approach Considered

Two approaches were considered:

**Option A (chosen)**: Exclude `status: "done"` from the transcript freshness guard. Minimal change, low risk.

**Option B (not chosen)**: Fix the persistence ordering so transcript mtime never exceeds registry `updatedAt`. This addresses the root cause (filesystem I/O timing), but involves more code paths and complexity. The persistence ordering issue is a known technical debt that could be addressed as a follow-up for other terminal states.

Option A was chosen because:
- It directly fixes the user-facing bug with minimal risk
- It follows the established pattern of excluding `failure` (same exclusion approach)
- The guard remains active for abnormal terminal states (`killed`, `timeout`, `endedAt-only`) where transcript-continuity recovery logic is still important
- A follow-up fix for persistence ordering would benefit all terminal states uniformly

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Successful main-agent sessions will no longer unexpectedly roll over to a new session ID when the transcript mtime is slightly newer than the registry `updatedAt`. The `.jsonl.reset.*` archive pattern will no longer appear for normal successful runs.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Regression Test Plan

- Updated existing test expectation in `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` for `status: "done"` case (now expects reuse instead of rotation)
- Updated existing test expectation in `src/commands/agent.session.test.ts` for `status: "done"` cases (now expects reuse)
- Updated existing test expectation in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` for the default-done case
- `endedAt-only` test cases unchanged (still assert rotation — guard remains active)
- All 3 affected test suites pass

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: status-done with newer transcript (reuse), endedAt-only with newer transcript (rotation), failed with newer transcript (reuse, unchanged), killed/timeout with newer transcript (rotation, unchanged)
- Edge cases checked: main session aliases (canonical, raw, custom) with done status; explicit session-id resume still works
- What you did NOT verify: Full Gateway E2E; real agent run producing the mtime ordering race

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only relaxes session reuse, never tightens
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The shared guard function is the right boundary because all three affected call paths (gateway, CLI, auto-reply) already depend on it. Adding the condition inline is minimal and follows the existing `failed` exclusion pattern.
- **Refactor needed**: No. A follow-up to fix persistence ordering (Option B) could be filed separately.
- **Alternative considered**: Fix persistence ordering so `updatedAt >= transcript mtime`. This is a deeper fix but involves more risk and wasn't necessary for this bug.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Lowest risk**: Only relaxes the guard for successful completions (`status: "done"`). Abnormal terminal states (`killed`, `timeout`, `endedAt-only`) remain fully guarded.
- **Familiar pattern**: Follows the exact same approach as the existing `failed` exclusion.
- **Test coverage**: All 3 call paths covered by existing tests, with updated expectations for the new behavior.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

Fixes #99964
