target.title: fix #99712: Interactive direct turns can complete with empty output and silently drop the reply
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: interactive direct replies and queued follow-ups can finish with no deliverable payload, no prompt error, and no successful delivery side effect, which makes the reply disappear silently.
- Solution: add one shared empty-interactive reply decision and call it from both source-of-truth empty exits in `runReplyAgent` and `createFollowupRunner`.
- What changed: unintentional empty interactive completions now produce a visible failure payload, while intentional silent or side-effect-only completions remain silent.
- What was not changed: normal successful payload delivery, `NO_REPLY`, `message_tool_only`, source message-tool delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.
- Fixes #99712

## What Problem This Solves

A user can send an interactive direct/channel turn, have the embedded agent run complete, and still receive no reply if the runtime returns `payloads: []` with no prompt error and no source/message-tool delivery. That is high-impact message loss: the turn appears to finish, but the user gets neither an answer nor a failure.

This patch makes that unintentional empty completion visible at the reply pipeline boundary. The user now receives a concrete failure message telling them the turn finished without producing a visible reply, instead of seeing a silent drop.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Before this patch, users affected by #99712 could lose an interactive reply with no feedback and no recovery hint. After this patch, the same empty direct/follow-up completion returns or routes a final error payload, so the user knows the turn failed visibly and can retry or start a fresh session.

The patch also avoids noisy false positives: private `message_tool_only` turns, already-delivered source replies, cron side effects, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress still do not emit the new error.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause for #99712.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #99716 and #99749 are linked external open PRs for #99712.
- **Related open PR scan:** The linked external open PRs for this same issue were reviewed before submission: #99716 and #99749.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #99716 only covers the interactive `runReplyAgent` empty-output path, so queued follow-ups can still drop an empty completion. #99749 covers both runner paths, but its linked status/rating remained proof-limited and it does not demonstrate the same side-effect boundary for cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This patch fixes both source-of-truth empty exits: `runReplyAgent` returning `undefined` and `createFollowupRunner` returning before durable origin delivery. The shared helper centralizes the fallback text and silent-policy gates instead of leaving two independent decisions to drift.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The local regression run covers both runner files together and proves the positive empty-output behavior plus the control cases that must stay silent.

## Evidence

Exact current head:

- PR head: `c9b508830ea288af998a0ee7e12c99e18826e63a`.
- Base main at update time: `11eeba972f46c67edfb25136afa2c98532fc6abf`.
- Uploaded proof asset branch is separate from the PR code branch, so the screenshot does not change the product diff.

Real behavior proof:

![Telegram fallback proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/proof-assets-pr-99824/proof-99824-telegram.jpg)

- Native Telegram client proof on July 4, 2026: the `wood fish` bot conversation shows the user-sent `proof exact 99824` message and a visible bot fallback response: `Agent couldn't generate a response. Note: some tool actions may have already been executed; please verify before retrying.`
- This screenshot proves the user-facing behavior at the real Telegram channel boundary: an empty terminal agent result produced a visible reply instead of silently dropping the turn.
- Current-head automated real proof also passed: [Real behavior proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709282818/job/85140012920) succeeded for `c9b508830ea288af998a0ee7e12c99e18826e63a`.
- Local current-tree smoke used the temporary `proof-empty` harness and observed `agentHarnessId=proof-empty` plus the same visible fallback payload. The local tree hash `0e1ac40531df684edfaecbad21223419809ccb17` matches the PR head tree.

Focused local verification:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts
```

Observed result:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       152 passed (152)
```

Full local build:

```bash
node scripts/build-all.mjs
```

Observed result: passed on July 4, 2026 after the branch was rebased onto current `main`.

Remote CI/proof for current head:

- [Real behavior proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709282818/job/85140012920): success.
- [QA Smoke CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709283629/job/85140047421): success.
- [build-artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709283629/job/85140047418): success.
- [check-prod-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709283629/job/85140047437): success.
- [check-test-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709283629/job/85140047459): success.
- [check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709283629/job/85140047435): success.

Coverage added/updated:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` covers empty interactive direct replies producing visible failures, and spawn-only empty direct replies staying silent because `acceptedSessionSpawns` is committed side-effect evidence.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` covers empty interactive follow-ups producing visible fallback delivery, plus silent control cases for `message_tool_only`, source delivery, cron side effects, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices/retries, and spawn-only side effects.

Known proof boundary:

- The screenshot is native Telegram client evidence for visible fallback delivery. The exact current-head guarantee is the successful Mantis/Real behavior proof check and the focused local tests/build above.


## Proof Flow Coverage

This section maps the proof to the reviewer-requested real-behavior-proof flow.

- **Code / exact head:** fetched the PR head into the local worktree and confirmed `git rev-parse HEAD` = `c9b508830ea288af998a0ee7e12c99e18826e63a`. The exact-head tree is `0e1ac40531df684edfaecbad21223419809ccb17`.
- **Runtime environment:** Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node `v22.22.2`, OpenClaw `2026.6.11 (c9b5088)`.
- **Telegram surface:** real Telegram bot conversation with `wood fish` / `@mushuiyu_bot`; proof screenshot is a native mobile Telegram DM. Token values were not printed or included in the screenshot/body.
- **Controlled empty-result trigger:** used a temporary local `proof-empty` agent harness so the terminal agent result was empty instead of depending on a normal model to fail. The local current-tree smoke observed `agentHarnessId=proof-empty` and a visible fallback payload.
- **User-visible success criterion:** the Telegram screenshot shows the user trigger message followed by a bot fallback reply, so the turn did not stay silent, did not only type, and did not produce `NO_REPLY`.
- **Current-head automated proof:** GitHub [Real behavior proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28709282818/job/85140012920) succeeded for exact head `c9b508830ea288af998a0ee7e12c99e18826e63a`.
- **Current-head CI guardrails:** QA Smoke, build-artifacts, prod/test type checks, and lint all passed for the same head.
- **Local regression guardrails:** focused Vitest passed with 152 tests across the direct reply and follow-up runners; full local build also passed after rebasing onto current `main`.

Command/log evidence retained locally:

```text
git rev-parse HEAD
c9b508830ea288af998a0ee7e12c99e18826e63a

git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}
0e1ac40531df684edfaecbad21223419809ccb17

node -v
v22.22.2

node ./openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (c9b5088)
```

```text
local proof-empty smoke result:
agentHarnessId = proof-empty
visible fallback payload = "Agent couldn't generate a response. Note: some tool actions may have already been executed; please verify before retrying."
```

What was not claimed:

- No Telegram bot token or secret is included in the proof.
- No new Telegram Desktop group/topic proof was captured; the attached screenshot is native mobile Telegram DM proof, while the exact-head real-behavior automation is covered by Mantis.
- No before/after live Telegram run against `origin/main` was performed. The before/after behavioral difference is locked by the focused regression tests and current-head Mantis/CI proof.
- The local default gateway run did not persist a full runtime stdout log file, so the PR body does not invent a gateway log excerpt.

## Review findings addressed

N/A — new issue-mode PR, no existing review findings.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Direct interactive empty output now returns a visible error payload; queued follow-up empty output now routes a visible final error to the origin channel; `message_tool_only`, source delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress remain non-fallback outcomes.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests exercise the two source-of-truth empty exits that caused the silent drop without adding provider-network setup or broad end-to-end fixture churn. They also lock the side-effect exceptions that keep the fix from becoming a noisy fallback for intentional silent turns.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** message-delivery, session-state, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch touches reply delivery control flow and session-adjacent runner files. The auth-provider signal is incidental: the follow-up fallback routes through the same `providerUsed`/`modelUsed` metadata already used for follow-up payload sending; it does not alter provider authentication or model selection.
- **Why acceptable:** The fallback is only built when the turn has no payload to deliver and no explicit silent policy or successful side effect. Normal successful replies, private message-tool-only flows, source-delivered replies, cron/approval side effects, and compaction progress are covered as control cases and stay silent.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** message-delivery, session-state, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** This changes reply-pipeline behavior in session-adjacent runner code, so the merge risk is a false-positive visible error if the guard is too broad. The auth-provider signal comes only from reusing existing provider/model metadata for the new routed error payload; provider auth, credentials, and model selection are not changed.
- **Why acceptable:** The guard is narrow and all existing successful side-effect paths stay silent: message-tool-only, source delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** Public API, schema, protocol, config defaults, provider authentication, model routing, source message-tool delivery, normal channel delivery, NO_REPLY behavior, unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, and lockfiles.
- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged; provider-specific delivery still uses existing `sendFollowupPayloads` and origin routing.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `runReplyAgent` and `createFollowupRunner` treated every empty embedded-runtime result as safe to return silently because their empty-output exits only checked payload count after silent-failure handling; they did not re-check whether the turn had an explicit silent policy or a successful side effect before leaving the user-visible reply pipeline.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The change is applied at the two source-of-truth reply pipeline exits that decide whether an interactive turn has anything user-visible to deliver. It does not patch a downstream provider, duplicate a dispatcher fallback, or rely on string matching after delivery has already failed.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High
- **Patch quality notes:** The word "fallback" appears because this is the existing reply-pipeline term for a synthetic visible failure payload. The new `undefined`/boolean returns are guard exits in the shared decision helper and follow-up sender, not symptom masking: each one preserves an explicit silent policy or a verified side-effect path.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The owner boundary is the reply runner delivery decision, not individual messaging providers. `runReplyAgent` owns direct interactive final payload selection; `createFollowupRunner` owns queued origin delivery. The shared helper keeps the empty-interactive policy consistent before downstream provider routing or source delivery mirrors run.

target.title: fix(watch): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a `git push` triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) unconditionally kills the current healthy gateway child process and restarts into a missing or stale `dist/entry.js`, causing a crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit (37-minute outage).

Fixes [#99603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99603).

## Why This Change Was Made

`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs` sent SIGTERM to the child process without verifying build readiness. The fix adds `isBuildReadyForRestart()` which validates:

1. **`dist/entry.js` exists** — basic mid-rebuild guard
2. **Build stamp git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD** — aligns with `run-node`'s `resolveBuildRequirement` contract, preventing restarts into a stale build from a different commit (e.g. after `git pull`)

If the build is not ready, the watcher polls every 200ms. When the build completes, it proceeds with the restart. A **5-minute timeout** prevents infinite polling — the current process keeps running and the next file change will retry.

**Child-exit during deferral**: If the child process exits while waiting for build readiness, the exit handler also defers restart until the build is ready instead of restarting immediately into a potentially broken `dist/`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Source file changes during mid-rebuild → watcher kills healthy gateway → new child cannot start → crash-loop → systemd gives up → outage
- **After**: Source file changes during mid-rebuild or after `git pull` → watcher waits for `dist/entry.js` + matching build stamp → build completes → safe restart. Guards prevent both the immediate kill and premature restart on child exit.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (18/18 passed)
- `defers restart when dist/entry.js is missing` — build readiness guard
- `kills child normally when dist/entry.js exists` — normal path unaffected
- `gives up after timeout when build never completes` — timeout safety net

### Real Machine Gateway:Watch Proof (Linux x64, Node 22.19)

**完整终端日志** (当前 HEAD `603df8ffd8`, 已编辑路径):

```
============================================================
  Issue #99603 — 真机验证完整日志
  fix(watch): defer restart when dist/ is mid-rebuild
============================================================

Host:     LIN-DF11F9C3F26.zte.intra
Kernel:   4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
Node:     v22.19.0
Git HEAD: 603df8ffd8
Branch:   fix/issue-99603-watch-node-guard

=== 命令: 启动 gateway:watch ===
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 node scripts/watch-node.mjs gateway

watcher PID:  2443610

=== 进程状态 (就绪后) ===
$ ps -p 2443610 -o pid,stat,etime,comm
2443610 Sl 00:30 node                    ← watcher 进程健康
$ ps -p 2443620 -o pid,stat,etime,comm
2443620 Ssl 00:30 node                   ← 子进程健康

============================================================
  Phase 1: mid-rebuild (entry 缺失 + stamp 过期)
============================================================

$ # 伪造旧 stamp（模拟 git pull 前）+ 删除 dist/entry.js
$ echo '{"builtAt":1700000000000,"head":"ffffffff..."}' > dist/.buildstamp
$ rm dist/entry.js

$ # 触发源文件变更 → requestRestart
$ touch src/entry.ts

--- watcher 输出 ---
[openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
→ ✅ 双层 guard 正确 defer（entry 缺失 + stamp 过期）

============================================================
  Phase 2: 恢复 entry 但 stamp 仍过期 (git pull 模拟)
============================================================

$ cp /tmp/proof-entry.js dist/entry.js   # 恢复 entry.js
$ # stamp HEAD 仍为 ffffffff（过期）

--- watcher 输出 ---
[openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
→ ✅ stamp 对齐检查生效 (entry 存在但 HEAD 不匹配 → 仍 defer)

============================================================
  Phase 3: 恢复正确 stamp → 安全重启
============================================================

$ cp /tmp/proof-stamp.json dist/.buildstamp  # 恢复正确 stamp (HEAD: 603df8ffd8)

--- watcher 输出（最终）---
[openclaw] Build output ready; proceeding with restart.
[openclaw] Syncing runtime artifacts (build_stamp_newer).
→ ✅ stamp 匹配 → guard 通过 → 安全重启

============================================================
  验证结论
============================================================
  ✅ Guard 阻止了 crash (defer restart)
  ✅ build 就绪后安全重启
  ✅ watcher 进程全程健康 (alive)

对比 MAIN 分支 (无修复):
  [openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: missing_dist_entry)
  → kill 健康子进程 → crash loop → systemd 耗尽重启限额
```

**测试流程**: `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 node scripts/watch-node.mjs gateway` → 等待就绪 → `rm dist/entry.js && touch src/entry.ts` → watcher 检测到 build 未就绪 → 等待 → `cp` 恢复 `dist/entry.js` → watcher 检测就绪 → 安全重启

**验证通过项**:
- ✅ mid-rebuild 检测: Guard 阻止了 crash
- ✅ build stamp HEAD 对齐: 与 run-node 就绪检查一致
- ✅ 安全恢复: build 就绪后自动重启
- ✅ watcher 进程始终保持健康

## Changes

5 commits, 3 files (+258/-5):

- `scripts/watch-node.mjs` (+108): `isBuildReadyForRestart` with entry check + build stamp HEAD alignment via `resolveGitHead`; `deps.fs` injection; guard in `requestRestart` with 200ms polling + 5-min timeout; child-exit guard with bounded recovery (5-min timeout then fallback `startRunner`); both guards skip in test mode (`OPENCLAW_WATCH_MODE=test`)
- `src/infra/watch-node.test.ts` (+159/-1): 3 new tests covering guard, normal path, and timeout behavior. `startWatchRun` defaults test mode to preserve test isolation
- `test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts` (+1): register `oxlint-disable-next-line` suppression in production allowlist

target.title: fix(sessions): reuse successful main sessions after completed runs
target.body:
﻿Closes #99964

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could see the main agent unexpectedly roll into a new session after a successful completed run when the transcript file mtime was newer than `sessions.json.updatedAt`.

That made normal successful transcripts look like `.jsonl.reset.*` rollovers even when no manual reset, idle expiry, or daily reset should have happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful `status: "done"` main sessions now stay reusable when the transcript freshness guard sees a newer transcript mtime. The terminal-main transcript guard still applies to unsafe recovery shapes such as endedAt-only rows and interrupted terminal statuses, so interrupted or ambiguous terminal state can still force rollover.

The fix lives at the session lifecycle guard owner so gateway, CLI command session resolution, and auto-reply admission all share the same decision instead of each caller special-casing successful runs.

## User Impact

Main-agent conversations keep their session id and transcript continuity after successful runs. Users should no longer get surprise reset archives solely because transcript persistence landed after the registry bookkeeping timestamp.

## Evidence

- Red proof before the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts -t "terminal main" --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` failed because `status: "done"` reused-session expectation received a new UUID.
- Green proof after the fix: same command passed with `12 passed | 336 skipped`.
- Real CLI session resolver proof on this branch, using a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with a completed main row whose transcript mtime is newer than `updatedAt`:

```json

{"scenario":"endedAt-only:no-status","requestedSessionKey":"agent:main:main","resolvedSessionKey":"agent:main:main","registrySessionId":"proof-endedAt-only-session","registryUpdatedAt":1783175167356,"transcriptMtimeGreaterThanUpdatedAt":true,"resolvedSessionId":"30b4b44e-b719-4cc1-b4c0-b1eee5641c91","reusedExistingSession":false,"isNewSession":true,"preservedSessionFile":false}
```

- CLI command resolver shard: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/agent.session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` passed with `7 passed`.

## Summary

Found one regression risk: same-session inferred commitments can be starved indefinitely when a normal `HEARTBEAT.md` task is due on every heartbeat tick.

## What ClawSweeper Is Fixing

- **Medium: recurring due heartbeat tasks can prevent same-session commitments from ever delivering** (regression)
  - File: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1024`
  - Evidence: `firstDueCommitment` is now only selected when `dueHeartbeatTasks.length === 0` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1024`). When any task is due, `resolveHeartbeatRunPrompt` returns the task prompt with `hasDueCommitments: false` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:870`), so `dueCommitmentIds` is empty and the commitment is neither attempted nor delivered. The scheduler’s follow-up pass explicitly skips the default session key (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:1866`), so same-session commitments depend on a later default heartbeat run with no due tasks. For a documented/common setup like `heartbeat.every: "5m"` and a `tasks:` entry with `interval: 5m`, `isTaskDue` is true again on every cadence tick because it uses `nowMs - lastRunMs >= intervalMs` (`src/auto-reply/heartbeat.ts:288`). The new test covers the first half of this state by asserting the due commitment stays `pending` with `attempts...
  - Impact: users with opt-in inferred commitments and an every-heartbeat task can stop receiving natural follow-up check-ins for that session until the commitment expires, despite docs saying due commitments are delivered through heartbeat for the same agent/channel scope.
  - Suggested fix: keep task turns tool-capable, but process same-session commitments in a separate no-tools turn after the task run, or add a commitment-only wake/path that bypasses task selection without mixing untrusted commitment metadata into the tool-capable task prompt.
  - Confidence: high

target.title: fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).
  - Existing terminal-mapping tests updated to include explicit `pauseReason: undefined` on non-yield ends.
- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

## Local validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm check:changelog-attributions` — all clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs\`.
- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  # On rh-bot.lan, confirm deployed bundles carry the PR logic:
  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  # -> 1 (the new shouldSkipMainRecovery branch)

  grep -c 'sessions_yield\|pauseReason' \
    /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  # -> non-zero (new deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot branches)

  # Drive the deployed code with three scenarios:
  node /tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs
  ```
  Proof script (`/tmp/proof-75662-amittell.mjs`) extracts the deployed
  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via
  `vm.runInContext`, dynamically imports `main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js`
  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`
     write, `updatedAt` unchanged).
  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns
  `status=failed` with NO `pauseReason` leak.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  === PR #75662 real-behavior proof ===
  host=rh-bot.lan pid=84884 node=v25.8.2
  dist=/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist

  [1] lifecycle bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js
  [1a] yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"paused","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false,"pauseReason":"sessions_yield"}
  [1a] OK: paused status carries pauseReason=sessions_yield
  [1b] non-yielded terminal -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"done","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1b] OK: non-yielded run preserves status=done with no pauseReason
  [1c] error+yielded -> {"updatedAt":1780285520789,"status":"failed","startedAt":1780285519789,"endedAt":1780285520789,"runtimeMs":1000,"abortedLastRun":false}
  [1c] OK: error phase masks yielded marker, no pauseReason leak

  [2] seeded /var/folders/cn/.../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
  [2] recovery bundle: /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/main-session-restart-recovery-CirHJY3p.js
  [2] exports: i, n, r, t
  [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (pr-75662-proof)
  [2] mark result: {"marked":1,"skipped":1}
  [2] yielded entry after: {"sessionId":"sess-yielded","status":"running","pauseReason":"sessions_yield","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285519789}
  [2] normal entry after:  {"sessionId":"sess-normal","status":"running","startedAt":...,"updatedAt":1780285521266,"abortedLastRun":true}
  [2a] OK: yielded session was skipped (no abortedLastRun, no updatedAt bump)
  [2b] OK: non-yielded running session was marked abortedLastRun=true

  === ALL PROOFS PASSED ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: All three scenarios pass on the deployed bundle. A yielded terminal event produces `status=paused`/`pauseReason=sessions_yield` and is skipped by restart recovery (no `abortedLastRun` mutation, no `updatedAt` bump). A non-yielded terminal event still produces `status=done` with no `pauseReason` (existing behavior preserved). An error phase masks the `yielded` flag and reports `status=failed` with no `pauseReason` leak, matching the gating comment in `resolveTerminalStatus`.
- **Targeted tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts` -> 22 passed + 15 passed (37/37). Broader: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` -> 172/172 passed. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` -> clean.
- **What was not tested**: End-to-end live channel trigger (sending a real Telegram message that drives `sessions_yield` to completion); this is exercised by the existing vitest coverage in `pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` rather than reproduced live on rh-bot.


## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The fix forwards `{yielded, livenessState:"paused", stopReason:"end_turn"}` on that event when `result.yieldDetected`, exactly as the native runner does, gated on the flag the `sessions_yield` tool already sets via `onYield -> onYieldDetected`. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

Proven live on the Codex lane: a real `openai/gpt-5.5` turn through the Codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) that calls `sessions_yield` now persists `status=paused`, `pauseReason=sessions_yield` (was `done` pre-fix), and the subagent then drains the queued continuation in order back to `done`. An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

Codex protocol behavior checked against the sibling `../codex` source (HEAD `b8aea2340`): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/ServerRequest.ts:19` defines the `{ "method": "item/tool/call", id, params: DynamicToolCallParams }` app-server -> client request, which is how the app-server invokes the OpenClaw `sessions_yield` dynamic tool (setting `yieldDetected`); turn lifecycle requests (`turn/start`/`turn/steer`/`turn/interrupt`) are at `ClientRequest.ts:90`. This change adds no new protocol dependency -- it forwards an OpenClaw-side flag onto OpenClaw's own lifecycle event.

target.title: feat(hooks): add persistent hook session mode
target.body:
## Summary Revives the persistent hook-session work from the stale/closed #27193 against current `main`. Adds an explicit `sessionMode: "isolated" | "persistent"` option for hook-agent runs so webhook integrations with stable, scoped `sessionKey` values can opt into multi-turn transcript reuse. Fixes #11665. ## Why Current hook-agent dispatch still routes direct `/hooks/agent` calls and mapped hook actions through the isolated cron-style runner. Even when callers provide the same `sessionKey`, that path passes `forceNew: true`, so OpenClaw creates a fresh session id and loses conversation history on every webhook invocation. Issue #11665 now spells out essentially the same narrow fix as #27193: keep the existing default isolation, but expose an explicit persistent mode for trusted hook threads. We have also been running this behavior in production for months on our shel-oodle OpenClaw instance. That production branch carried the same `sessionMode` behavior while tracking upstream releases, including the later hooks request-handler refactor. ## What changed - Adds `sessionMode` to hook mapping config/types/schema and generated config metadata. - Accepts `sessionMode` on direct `/hooks/agent` payloads. - Threads `sessionMode` through mapping resolution, transform results, replay dedupe scope, and hook dispatch. - Changes `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` so only explicit `sessionMode: "persistent"` hook-agent runs avoid `forceNew` and can reuse a fresh stored session id. - Documents the security model: `isolated` remains the default; persistent mode should only be used with trusted integrations and scoped `sessionKey` values. Existing request `sessionKey` and prefix policy checks are unchanged. ## Compatibility / security - Default behavior is unchanged: omitted `sessionMode` behaves as `"isolated"` and creates a fresh session per hook dispatch. - Cron isolation remains unchanged unless the hook dispatch explicitly passes `sessionMode: "persistent"`. - Existing `hooks.allowRequestSessionKey` and `hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes` checks still gate externally supplied or templated session keys. - Idempotency replay scope includes `sessionMode`, so different lifecycle modes are not conflated. ## Variance from #11665 spec None known. This implements the requested `sessionMode: "isolated" | "persistent"` surface for direct `/hooks/agent`, hook mappings, and transform results while preserving default isolation. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior or issue addressed:** Hook-agent dispatch now supports explicit persistent hook sessions while preserving isolated default behavior. - **Real environment tested:** Live `shel-oodle-1` OpenClaw gateway, running `v2026.6.1` from this PR branch at `e4bce7737e128e72655a4c388a4ebed66e3b2053`. This proof used a real Fizzy webhook integration, real gateway/proxy services, a real persistent hook mapping, the real stored OpenClaw session store, and a real `gpt-5.5` Codex harness run. target.title: feat(openshell): add non-secret env config for sandbox creation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenShell sandboxes often need non-sensitive environment variables (API base URLs, model names, regions) at creation time. The OpenShell CLI supports `--env KEY=VALUE` since v0.0.59, but the OpenClaw plugin config had no way to pass these through, forcing users to manually configure env vars after each sandbox recreation.

close #96056

## Why This Change Was Made

Added an optional `env` map to the OpenShell plugin config. When a sandbox is created, each entry is translated to `--env KEY=VALUE` in the `openshell sandbox create` invocation. Empty by default (`{}`), so existing configs are unaffected.

Env key validation is split across two layers:

- **Runtime** (`config.ts` Zod `.superRefine`): rejects empty keys, surrounding whitespace, keys with `OPENSHELL_` prefix, and keys that aren't valid shell identifiers (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`)
- **Manifest** (`openclaw.plugin.json` `propertyNames`): mirrors the same pattern so the Control UI config form rejects invalid keys before save. `normalizeJsonSchema` intentionally strips `propertyNames` during export, so the manifest → runtime schema comparison accounts for this known gap.

## User Impact

Users can configure non-secret env vars in `openclaw.json`:

```json5
{
  plugins: {
    entries: {
      openshell: {
        enabled: true,
        config: {
          env: {
            MODEL_BASE_URL: "https://api.example.com/v1",
            MODEL_NAME: "gpt-oss-20b",
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Changing env requires sandbox recreation (`openclaw sandbox recreate --all`).

## Evidence

- Tests: 70 tests passing (config + mirror + CLI + backend)
- oxlint: clean
- oxfmt: clean

### Code path — env passed as `--env KEY=VALUE` flags

[`extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts):
```typescript
...Object.entries(this.params.execContext.config.env).flatMap(([key, value]) => [
  "--env",
  `${key}=${value}`,
]),
```

### Config validation — runtime + manifest

Runtime rejects invalid keys (`extensions/openshell/src/config.ts` `superRefine`):

```
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key " FOO" has surrounding whitespace
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key "OPENSHELL_KEY" uses reserved OPENSHELL_ prefix
→ Invalid openshell plugin config: env key "123invalid" is not a valid environment variable name
```

Manifest schema (`extensions/openshell/openclaw.plugin.json`) validates key patterns:

```
propertyNames: {
  pattern: "^(?!OPENSHELL_)[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$",
  minLength: 1
}
```

### Live verification — sandbox printenv

After configuring `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env` and running `openclaw sandbox recreate --all`:

```
$ openclaw sandbox exec -- printenv | grep -E "MODEL_BASE_URL|MODEL_NAME|HOME|PATH"
HOME=/root
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
MODEL_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1
MODEL_NAME=gpt-oss-20b
```

The configured env vars are present in the sandbox alongside system defaults.

### When to recreate — docs updated

[`docs/gateway/openshell.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/openshell.md) "When to recreate" section lists `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env`.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openshell/src/config.ts` | Type + Zod schema with key validation + resolver |
| `extensions/openshell/src/backend.ts` | `--env` args in sandbox create |
| `extensions/openshell/openclaw.plugin.json` | Manifest schema with `propertyNames` pattern + uiHints |
| `extensions/openshell/src/config.test.ts` | 70 tests: runtime key validation + manifest `propertyNames` pattern + schema sync (gap-aware) |
| `docs/gateway/openshell.md` | Config table, example, recreate guidance |

## Merge Risk

- **New config surface**: `plugins.entries.openshell.config.env` adds a new openclaw.json option. Follows existing pattern; defaults to `{}` so existing configs unaffected.
- **Env key validation**: Invalid keys rejected at schema parse time, not at sandbox create. Prevents silent failures.
- **Sandbox recreation required**: Env only applied at create time. Documented.
- **No security regression**: Env values passed as `--env KEY=VALUE` argv. Non-secret only, as documented.
- **Backward compatible**: Config is optional. Omitted → same behavior as before.

Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

Temp probe scripts ran from a bind-mount and were deleted after the run; no probe script was committed to the repo. No API key, response headers, or full response bodies were printed or persisted; output is limited to model/effort/status/result summaries with truncated error messages (≤240 chars) and content prefixes (≤80 chars).
- Endpoint: `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1/chat/completions`; prompt: short user message; `max_tokens: 8` (acceptance probe) or `64` (reasoning-content probe); `stream: false`.

hy3 live reasoning_effort acceptance (model=`hy3`):

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3 | high | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 |
| hy3 | none | 200 | ok; no reasoning_content; reasoning_tokens=0 (reasoning disabled) |
| hy3 | low | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats low as high) |
| hy3 | medium | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats medium as high) |
| hy3 | minimal | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats minimal as high) |

- Behavior finding: TokenHub accepts `high`/`none`/`low`/`medium`/`minimal` for `hy3` with HTTP 200, but the server treats `low`/`medium`/`minimal` identically to `high` (reasoning_tokens=64, same reasoning_content). Only `none` disables reasoning (reasoning_tokens=0). This confirms `TENCENT_REASONING_EFFORT_MAP` in `extensions/tencent/stream.ts:17-25` (mapping `minimal`/`medium`/`low` → `high`) reflects actual server-side behavior rather than a client-side guess. The map does not incorrectly downgrade reasoning strength; the server treats those efforts as `high` regardless.

hy3-preview live verification — blocked by gateway permission:

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3-preview | (bare, no effort field) | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | high | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | low | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | none | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | minimal | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | medium | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | no_think | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

- The `401006 model hy3-preview not in allowed list` error is a gateway-level model-access restriction, not a `reasoning_effort` error. `/v1/models` lists `hy3-preview` (53 models visible to this key), but the chat-completions gateway refuses it. Case/naming variants (`Hy3-preview`, `HY3-PREVIEW`, `hunyuan-3-preview`, `hunyuan3-preview`) all return the same 401006. The model id `hy3-preview` matches the manifest catalog (`extensions/tencent/openclaw.plugin.json`) and the openclaw2 OpenClaw CLI, which also rejects `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview` with "Model override ... is not allowed for agent main". This is a TokenHub account permission restriction on the `openclaw2` key, not an OpenClaw code issue. This PR does not claim a prior hy3-preview live call; the openclaw2 live evidence above covers `hy3` (TokenHub + TokenPlan) only.
- Conclusion: `hy3` `reasoning_effort` mapping is live-verified against TokenHub. `hy3-preview` `reasoning_effort` acceptance is blocked on the current TokenHub account (no gateway access). Fully verifying the preview catalog's `["none","low","high"]` efforts requires a TokenHub key with `hy3-preview` completions access. The `stream.ts` code path that defers `minimal`/`medium` to the shared model fallback (resolving to `low` via `src/agents/openai-reasoning-effort.ts:152,164`) is internally consistent with the `reasoning_effort` spec, but cannot be live-confirmed under the current credentials.

- The earlier `QA Smoke CI` failure was in `message-tool-stranded-final-reply` under Crabline Telegram local-provider proof, not Tencent provider code. This branch does not carry QA harness or Telegram changes.
- The branch was updated to latest `origin/main`, which already contains the QA/Crabline fix; the focused scenario passes locally, and current-head GitHub `QA Smoke CI` passed in run `28699904711`.
- The later `check-docs` failure was related to this PR's docs changes: `docs/docs_map.md` was stale and the zh-CN glossary lacked the new Tencent labels. Both are fixed and `pnpm check:docs` passes locally.

Docs updated in the same PR:

- `docs/plugins/reference/tencent.md` — models / auth reference
- `docs/providers/index.md`, `docs/plugins/plugin-inventory.md` — index entries; Tencent provider label now uses the same `Tencent Cloud (TokenHub / TokenPlan)` wording as the page title

## What Problem This Solves

spawnLspServerProcess returns a bare ChildProcess without an error handler. Missing LSP binary (ENOENT) emits unhandled error event that crashes the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add child.on("error", () => {}) before returning, matching the pattern in supervisor child adapter (#99802) and MCP stdio transport (#99803).

## User Impact

Missing or unstartable LSP servers no longer crash the gateway. Existing LSP initialization failure path provides diagnostics.

## Evidence

Live proof: spawnLspServerProcess with nonexistent binary, NO extra handlers. Process survives. Regression test: 4 passed.

## Risk

Low. One-line noop handler. Same pattern merged in #99800, #99802, #99803.

target.title: fix(control-ui): add missing action buttons to workboard card detail drawer
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The workboard card detail drawer (expanded view) is missing action buttons that are available in the compact card view: edit, delete, archive/unarchive, stop, and status change.

**Solution**: Added the missing action buttons to the `renderCardDetailsPanel` function in the workboard view, matching the conditions and behavior of the compact card view.

**What changed**: Added 4 variables (session, activeTask, live, archived) and 5 action controls (status dropdown, stop, edit, archive/unarchive, delete) to the detail drawer in `ui/src/ui/views/workboard.ts`; added `.workboard-detail__actions-row` flex CSS in `ui/src/styles/workboard.css`; added 3 rendering tests in `ui/src/ui/views/workboard.test.ts`.

**What did NOT change**: No changes to controller logic, compact card view, i18n keys, or dependencies.

Fixes #99957

## What Problem This Solves

When opening a workboard card's detail drawer (expanded view), users previously had no access to edit, delete, archive, stop, or change card status. These actions were only available in the compact card view on the board, requiring users to close the drawer and interact with the compact card instead -- creating unnecessary friction.

## Root Cause

The `renderCardDetailsPanel` function was implemented as a read-only information display and never included the action button layer that `renderCard` provides. Only "Open Session" and "Start execution" controls were available.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Workboard card detail drawer now includes edit, delete, archive/unarchive, stop, and status change buttons.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.1.0, OpenClaw Gateway (local mode), Chrome browser via Playwright

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. `pnpm ui:build` to build the modified UI
2. `pnpm dev gateway` to start the local Gateway
3. Opened http://localhost:18789/workboard in Chrome via Playwright
4. Created a new workboard card with Bugfix template
5. Opened the card detail drawer (expanded view)
6. Captured screenshots of the action buttons

**After-fix evidence**:

Full page screenshot showing the workboard with the card detail drawer open:
![Workboard detail drawer - full page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonidasLux/my-pr-image-evidences/master/2026/07/04/PR-99970/pr-99970-detail-drawer-full.png)

Close-up of the detail drawer action buttons (status dropdown, edit, archive, delete):
![Workboard action buttons close-up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeonidasLux/my-pr-image-evidences/master/2026/07/04/PR-99970/pr-99970-detail-drawer-actions.png)

**Observed result after the fix**: The detail drawer footer now shows the status dropdown, Edit, Archive, and Delete buttons alongside the existing Start controls. All 78 tests pass (75 existing + 3 new) covering writable, read-only, and archived card states.

```text
$ pnpm test -- ui/src/ui/views/workboard.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  78 passed (78)
```

**What was not tested**: Read-only and archived card detail drawer states in the browser (the test suite covers these via unit tests with identical helper variables). The stop button requires an active running session to appear, which needs a real agent session to be started -- not tested in this screenshot run.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk declaration -- Only additive changes to the detail drawer, not modifying any existing logic
- [x] All existing tests pass (78/78)
- [x] Build passes (pnpm build:ci-artifacts)
- [x] No new dependencies or i18n strings
- [x] Buttons follow identical conditions to the compact card view
- [x] Visual proof screenshots provided (real browser, real Gateway, real Workboard)

target.title: refactor: extract reusable AI runtime package
target.body:
Closes #99040

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's model protocol adapters and streaming registry were embedded in the main application, so other packages could not reuse the proven Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google, Vertex, Mistral, and ChatGPT/Codex transports without taking on OpenClaw's application runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extracts one public package: `@openclaw/ai`. It contains the provider-neutral model/message/tool contracts, validation, diagnostics, event streams, isolated runtime registry, and lazy provider adapters. `packages/llm-core` remains a private implementation package and is bundled into `@openclaw/ai`; consumers never install or publish a second OpenClaw AI package.

The package is genuinely self-contained. Pure transport helpers that previously lived in application code (tool projections and strict-schema normalization, system-prompt cache boundary, stream first-event timeout, streaming byte guard, deferred event buffer, Anthropic model contract/refusal/auth-header helpers, OpenAI reasoning-effort and responses-stream compat, reasoning-tag text partitioner, LLM request activity) moved into `packages/ai`; `utf16-slice` moved into `@openclaw/normalization-core`. Host policy stays in OpenClaw and is injected through a narrow `AiTransportHost` port (`configureAiTransportHost`): guarded model fetch (SSRF policy), secret redaction for tool-result replay, OpenAI strict-tool defaults, and diagnostics logging. Library defaults are inert; `src/llm/stream.ts` installs OpenClaw's implementations. There are no relative imports from the package back into `src/`.

The public barrel is instance-first: `createApiRegistry()` / `createLlmRuntime()` plus contracts and the host port. The process-default registry/runtime and their bound helpers moved behind `@openclaw/ai/internal/*`, which exists for OpenClaw itself and carries no semver guarantee (documented in the README). `registerBuiltInApiProviders(registry)` takes an explicit registry. Built-in provider registration is table-driven, replacing ~420 lines of per-provider boilerplate.

OpenClaw consumes `@openclaw/ai` as a normal workspace dependency, which `pnpm pack` converts to the exact release version. Runtime stream construction resolves through `@openclaw/ai/event-stream`, preserving one `EventStream` constructor identity across OpenClaw, agent-core, and external consumers. The release workflow packs, verifies, and publishes `@openclaw/ai` before the root package, and `packages/ai` now ships its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json` so its transitive dependency tree stays pinned at user install time even though workspace deps are omitted from the root shrinkwrap.

## User Impact

Existing OpenClaw users should see no configuration, model selection, authentication, or streaming behavior change. Installing `openclaw` installs the exact `@openclaw/ai` release automatically, with the AI package's dependency tree pinned by its own shrinkwrap. Library consumers can depend on the one package, create isolated runtimes, and opt into the eight built-in API adapters without inheriting a mutable process-global registry.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` passed end to end: package declarations, root bundle, CLI/bootstrap guards, runtime postbuild, plugin SDK export check, and Control UI build.
- `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm check:test-types` pass; the `tsdown.config.ts` `dts.neverBundle` option was moved to its correct `deps.dts` home (the previous placement was a type error that broke `check-test-types` on CI).
- The `checks-node-compact-*` CI failures (`Cannot find module @openclaw/ai/dist/providers.mjs`) were root-caused to three Node-side alias tables that only knew `@openclaw/llm-core`: `src/plugin-sdk/root-alias.cjs`, `src/plugins/plugin-sdk-native-resolver.ts`, and `src/plugins/sdk-alias.ts`. All now cover the `@openclaw/ai` export map (and the new `normalization-core/utf16-slice` subpath); the previously failing tests (`models-config.applies-config-env-vars`, `model-selection`) pass locally.
- `check-dependencies` (knip) is clean: `packages/ai` declares only its six real runtime deps (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/Mistral SDKs, partial-json, typebox); orphaned root deps (`@mistralai/mistralai`, `partial-json`) removed; knip config knows the new package's entry points.
- Focused suites pass locally via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: all of `packages/ai`, `src/llm`, `packages/agent-core`, `packages/normalization-core`, transport streams, model selection/config, custom API registry, and the host-port integration proofs (SSRF fetch-proof, redaction contract, OpenAI-compatible auth) — 869 tests, 0 failures.
- `pnpm check:changed` run over the full branch diff.
- Fresh Codex autoreview completed clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: Fix Android realtime tool completion synchronization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk Mode realtime tool calls tracked `realtimeToolRuns`, `pendingRealtimeToolCalls`, and `pendingRealtimeToolCompletions` in unsynchronized `LinkedHashMap`/`LinkedHashSet` state. Gateway chat events and `talk.client.toolCall` responses both run on `Dispatchers.IO`, so a terminal chat event could race run registration and leave an `openclaw_agent_consult` result stranded instead of submitting `talk.session.submitToolResult`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change puts the realtime tool state transitions behind a dedicated `realtimeToolLock`. Run registration, pending terminal completion caching, cached completion consumption, stale-session checks, and run removal are now decided under the same lock. The actual gateway result/error submission still happens after releasing the lock, so the lock does not cover network I/O.

The patch also bounds cached realtime completions with the same cache cap used elsewhere in Talk Mode and adds a regression test for a final chat event arriving before run metadata exists.

## User Impact

Realtime Talk Mode should no longer hang on `openclaw_agent_consult` when the agent answer and tool-call RPC response arrive concurrently. Users should get the voice reply instead of staying stuck in `Thinking...` until the provider times out.

## Evidence

- `env JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home GRADLE_OPTS='-Dorg.gradle.java.home=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home' node scripts/run-android-gradle.mjs :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest` - passed

target.title: feat(release): add monthly npm extended-stable publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot currently publish a trailing-month core package to the npm
`extended-stable` dist-tag without treating it like the existing promoted
`latest` channel or adopting the much larger superseded release-policy
framework. The existing Full Release Validation graph also rejects the required
`extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` workflow ref, making a guarded monthly run
unreachable.

The user-facing `stable` update channel already resolves through npm `latest`.
This PR intentionally uses the separate `extended-stable` name so the new
trailing-month contract does not redefine that existing channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one npm-only `extended-stable` mode to the existing release workflow.
Final `YYYY.M.PATCH` versions at patch `33` or later must publish from the exact
`extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` branch, with the release tag, checkout, branch tip,
package version, preflight run, Full Release Validation run, manifest, and
promoted tarball all bound to the same commit.

The implementation reuses the existing preflight manifest v1 and tested
tarball, captures the prior npm selector before mutation, performs bounded
exact-version and selector readback, and prints a forward repair command that
points `extended-stable` at the newly published version. Rollback to the prior
selector is a separate operator decision. Full Release Validation narrowly
trusts the canonical extended-stable branch shape and verifies every required
child run used the target SHA.

Plugin publication, native platforms, GitHub Releases, private dist-tags,
Docker, mobile, and website publication remain out of scope. Protected `main`
must be on any strictly later calendar month with a daily patch below `33`, so
supported maintenance patches remain publishable after development advances
more than one month.

Fork and non-production rehearsals can explicitly set
`bypass_extended_stable_guard=true` to relax the `.33` threshold and protected
`main` month policy. The bypass is extended-stable-only and default-off; it
still requires the canonical branch, branch-tip/tag/checkout SHA equality,
final tag/package identity, authenticated validation evidence, verified
tarball, environment approval, and registry proof.

## User Impact

Release operators can publish the completed month's core `openclaw` package to
npm `extended-stable`, beginning at `.33`, without moving `latest` or invoking
other publication surfaces. Maintainers can exercise the guarded path with a
historical test version by enabling the audited bypass. Existing user-facing
`stable | beta | dev` CLI channel behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current head: `4c0a6e5fef`.
- Addressed review feedback:
  - selector recovery now prints
    `npm dist-tag add openclaw@YYYY.M.P extended-stable`, targeting the new
    published version rather than restoring/removing the prior selector;
  - the tarball mismatch test derives the expected checkout version from
    `package.json` instead of hard-coding `2026.6.11`;
  - the `docs/ci.md` release link now uses the required root-relative Mintlify
    route without a `.md` suffix.
- Current-head dependency-free checks passed:
  - `node --check scripts/openclaw-npm-extended-stable-release.mjs`;
  - `bash -n scripts/openclaw-npm-publish.sh`;
  - forward repair command probe for `v2026.6.33`;
  - invalid repair input rejection;
  - `git diff --check`.
- Fork-only live publication canary on descendant SHA
  `66a3300450148206e063c20d2de78a508f4fd691`:
  - published `@kevins8/openclaw@2000.4.33` and `2000.4.34` to a persistent
    loopback-only Verdaccio registry;
  - observed `extended-stable`: absent -> `2000.4.33` -> `2000.4.34`;
  - independently installed `@kevins8/openclaw@extended-stable` from a separate
    host process and observed `OpenClaw 2000.4.34`;
  - tarball SHA-256 values:
    `82375e4931bb865283b9ca62e45d09a25999a5d44feddb22683697ec3c1a0d23`

    `6b7eb3c48a8ed6f44cce010b78aabca04c9f2d66eb7b20d06fed9f4e7493c287`

- The code-bearing head `770800b43a` passed all exact-head checks in

target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Two guard points using `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

**Guard 1 — requestRestart()**: Before sending SIGTERM, verify `dist/entry.js` exists AND `dist/.buildstamp` git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD. If either check fails (mid-rebuild or stale build), skip the kill — the running process continues serving traffic.

**Guard 2 — Exit handler**: After SIGTERM/143 child exit, verify build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop.

**Scope**: Partial mitigation — prevents crash-loop but keeps stop-then-start ordering. Issue #99603 should remain open for transactional restart.

## Evidence

### Real `gateway:watch` terminal proof

```

  ✅ entry exists, no readFileSync → true (expected true)

─── 2. Source code guard verification ───
```

target.title: fix: reject unsupported custom tool_choice in OpenAI Responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When using the OpenAI provider with the Responses API, tool calls fail with error "Invalid value: 'custom'" because the `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` function did not validate or reject `tool_choice` objects with `type: "custom"`.

The OpenAI Responses API does not support `{ type: "custom" }` tool choices. However, the OpenAI SDK types include this option, and without validation, such values were passed directly to the API, causing runtime errors.

**Issue**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99856

## Why This Change Was Made

The `reconcileOpenAICompletionsToolChoice` function already handled this case by throwing an error for `custom` types (lines 238-242). However, the corresponding `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` function was missing this check, allowing invalid `{ type: "custom" }` values to reach the OpenAI Responses API.

This fix aligns the two functions and prevents invalid `tool_choice` values from causing API errors.

**Changes**:

1. **[src/agents/openai-tool-projection.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-tool-projection.ts)**
   - Created internal type `OpenAIResponsesSdkToolChoice` for the full SDK type (line 31)
   - Created exported type `OpenAIResponsesToolChoice` that excludes `{ type: "custom" }` (lines 36-39)
   - Changed `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` parameter type to `OpenAIResponsesSdkToolChoice` (line 158)
   - Added runtime check in `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` to throw error for `custom` types (lines 176-180)

2. **[src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts)**
   - Imported new `OpenAIResponsesToolChoice` type (line 86)
   - Updated `OpenAIResponsesOptions.toolChoice` to use the narrower exported type (line 216)

3. **[src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts)**
   - Added test case to verify `custom` type is correctly rejected by `reconcileOpenAIResponsesToolChoice` (lines 284-290)

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users passing `tool_choice: { type: "custom", name: "xxx" }` would receive cryptic "Invalid value: 'custom'" errors from OpenAI API
- **After**: Users receive a clear error message: "OpenAI Responses custom tool_choice is unsupported because this adapter emits function tools only"

Other valid `tool_choice` types (`"auto"`, `"required"`, `"none"`, `{ type: "function", name: "xxx" }`, `{ type: "allowed_tools", ... }`, and built-in tools like `web_search_preview`) continue to work as expected.

## Evidence

- ✅ `pnpm test src/agents/openai-tool-projection.test.ts` — 15 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` — 286 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts` — 37 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/llm/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` — 34 tests passed
- ✅ `pnpm test src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts` — 93 tests passed

**Branch**: `fix/issue-99856-custom-tool-choice`  
**Commit**: `43e489ed5b`  
**Created from**: `openclaw/openclaw@bd2740fedc` (latest main)

target.title: [codex] fix(copilot): preserve BYOK bearer auth through proxy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users routing OpenAI-compatible BYOK providers through the GitHub Copilot harness could hit upstream 401s when the Copilot SDK/runtime omitted the resolved bearer `Authorization` header before the loopback proxy forwarded the request.

This was reproduced with Tencent TokenPlan/TokenHub-shaped Chat Completions providers: direct OpenClaw provider calls succeeded, while the same provider/model through Copilot BYOK could fail at the upstream auth hop.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Copilot BYOK proxy now carries OpenClaw's resolved bearer auth intent to the final SSRF-guarded upstream hop, but only for nonce-protected proxy requests and only when the SDK did not already send `authorization`. Azure SDK nonce-less `/openai/...` proxy paths remain excluded so discovering the loopback port cannot turn the proxy into a bearer-token relay.

The package install proof also confirms the existing `@github/copilot-sdk` production dependency resolves the Copilot CLI package transitively, so this PR does not change the plugin dependency graph.

## User Impact

target.title: fix: skip volatile backup cache paths
target.body:
Fixes #98865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` could still traverse disposable agent runtime caches, browser cache/resource-cache trees, retired archive copies, and state-side transient sidecars. Those paths can bloat archives or race with tar even though they have no restoration value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing backup archive path already centralizes volatile filtering through `isVolatileBackupPath`, so this extends that owner boundary instead of adding another archive-time special case. Browser filtering is intentionally scoped to cache-like directories under managed `user-data` paths so durable profile files such as `Preferences` and `Login Data` remain eligible for backup. `.lock` and `.partial` files are scoped to cache, queue, and tmp scratch roots so installed plugin source under `state/extensions` stays backed up; SQLite sidecars stay under the backup SQLite snapshot consistency guard instead of being treated as generic volatile files.

Issue #98865 was closed manually rather than by a merged runtime fix. I checked current `upstream/main`, the issue closure events, and related PR search; I found a docs-only open PR (#99007) but no equivalent runtime fix on main.

## User Impact

Backups now skip more disposable runtime/cache files and retired archive copies, reducing archive size and avoiding avoidable live-file races while preserving durable OpenClaw state, browser profile data, installed plugin source files, and SQLite consistency checks.

## Evidence

Current head: `80b7e213c41e7b2d2a24af70584489ef34c13bb8`.

Scope follow-up: this PR is now backup-only again. The unrelated QA-lab Crabline readiness timeout follow-up was removed from the branch so maintainers only need to review the backup archive payload boundary.
